chapter_title: I'm Up and Down, and Round and Round

concepts.title: Definition and Basic Properties of a Circle
concepts.definition: Mark every spot that sits one fixed gap away from a chosen mid-point; the round curve so formed is called a circle. Name that middle spot the centre, with the fixed gap as the radius.
concepts.key_idea: One fixed gap out of the mid-point explains the whole shape.
question_patterns: If the radius is 7 cm, state the diameter.
Calculate the diameter of a circle whose radius is 5.5 cm.
How does the width across a circle compare with its radius?
Double the radius of 9 cm - what do you get?
The radius grew from 4 cm to 10 cm; by how much did the full width grow?

solution_steps.explain: The full width across is twice the radius.
The centre is the fixed mid-point and the radius is the constant gap from centre to any point on the curve.
Every chord through the centre is a diameter and equals twice the radius, confirming the defining property of the circle.

concepts.title: Circumcircle of a Triangle
concepts.definition: Through any three spots that are not lined up, exactly one round curve can pass.
concepts.key_idea: The side bisectors (drawn square to their sides) meet where the curve's centre sits.
question_patterns: Show that exactly one round curve passes through three spots that are not lined up.
Construct the curve through the corners of a triangle.
Explain how the side bisectors locate the curve's centre.
Where does the centre sit for an acute triangle? And for an obtuse one?
Draw a triangle and verify that its three corners sit at one gap from the centre.

solution_steps.explain: Find the point O where the right-angle bisectors of two sides meet.
Show that O sits at the same gap from each corner A, B and C.
With O as centre and the common gap as radius, the round curve through A, B and C is the unique circumcircle.

concepts.title: Central Angles Subtended by Chords
concepts.definition: Chords of matching size pull equal corners out of the mid-point.
concepts.key_idea: Same size chord, same size centre-facing angle - and it works backwards too.
question_patterns: Show that matching chords make matching angles at the centre.
Prove the converse: chords facing equal central angles are equal.
Verify the claim for two chords of length 6 cm in one curve.
Draw two equal chords and measure the angles they make at the centre.
Justify the matching-angle claim using congruent triangles.

solution_steps.explain: Join both chords' ends to the centre O to build two triangles.
Two sides are radii and the third sides are equal chords, so the triangles match by SSS.
Corresponding parts of congruent triangles are equal, so the central angles subtended by equal chords are equal, and the converse holds by the same argument.

concepts.title: Chord Length from Radius and Distance from Centre
concepts.definition: Drop a square-corner line from the mid-point down onto any chord and it cuts the chord into two matching halves.
concepts.key_idea: The dropped line halves the chord; radius, half-chord and gap then make a right triangle.
question_patterns: Find the chord whose radius is 13 cm and whose gap from the centre is 5 cm.
Calculate the length cut when a chord sits 9 cm from the centre of a 15 cm curve.
What is the full chord when its half is 12 cm?
Compute the chord of a 10 cm curve whose gap is 6 cm.
State the theorem that lets a dropped centre line halve a chord.

solution_steps.action: Half chord via the right triangle
solution_steps.explain: Half the chord is a leg of a right triangle with the radius as the longest side.
The dropped line halves the chord, so the full length is twice the half.
The perpendicular from the centre to a chord always bisects it, which is why the right-triangle relation holds for every chord.

concepts.title: Radius of Circle from Chord Length and Distance
concepts.definition: Half a chord plus its gap out from the mid-point forms a right triangle; the radius plays the longest side.
concepts.key_idea: Add the squares of half-chord and gap, then take the root, to recover the radius.
question_patterns: Find the radius when a 16 cm chord sits 6 cm from the centre.
Calculate the radius for a 24 cm chord with a 5 cm gap.
What is the curve's size if half the chord is 12 cm and the gap is 9 cm?
Work out the radius from a 10 cm chord sitting 12 cm away.
Explain why the radius acts as the longest side in the chord triangle.

solution_steps.explain: The dropped line halves the chord.
Radius squared is half-chord squared plus gap squared.

solution_steps.action: Confirm the radius as the longest side
solution_steps.explain: The radius is the hypotenuse of the right triangle formed by the half-chord and the distance, so it is always longer than both the half-chord and the distance.

concepts.title: Angle Subtended by an Arc at Centre and Circumference
concepts.definition: The corner an arc makes at the middle spot is double the corner it makes at any other spot of the curve.
concepts.key_idea: Centre sees double: an on-curve angle is half the centre's angle.
question_patterns: An arc makes a 70 degree corner at the centre; find the corner it makes on the curve.
Calculate the on-curve angle when the centre angle is 120 degrees.
What on-curve angle goes with a straight 180 degree centre angle?
The centre angle tripled; what happens to the on-curve angle?
State the centre-to-curve angle rule for a fixed arc.

solution_steps.explain: The on-curve angle is half the centre angle for the same arc.

solution_steps.action: Identify the arc and the chosen on-curve spot
solution_steps.explain: The same arc subtends the central angle at the centre and the inscribed angle at any point on the remaining part of the curve.
The angle at the centre is always twice the angle at the circumference subtended by the same arc, which is why halving the central angle gives the inscribed angle.

concepts.title: Angle in a Semicircle
concepts.definition: Wherever a spot sits on the round curve, the corner made across a full width (a diameter) comes out a right angle.
concepts.key_idea: Every width-crossing corner on the curve is 90 degrees.
question_patterns: What is the corner made across a diameter at the curve?
Show that the corner in a half curve is a right angle.
A triangle pinned on the curve with one side a width: what type is the corner opposite that side?
Find the angle ACB when AB is a width and C sits on the curve.
Justify the right-angle claim with the centre-to-curve rule.

solution_steps.explain: A diameter makes a 180 degree angle at the centre.
The on-curve corner is half of 180, namely 90 degrees.

solution_steps.action: Confirm the right angle for any on-curve spot
solution_steps.explain: Since the diameter is a straight angle at the centre, every point on the curve sees it as a 90 degree angle, giving a right-angled triangle regardless of where the point sits.

concepts.title: Concyclic Points and Angles in Same Segment
concepts.definition: Matching corners over the same base line, seen from two spots on one side of it, force all four spots onto a single round curve.
concepts.key_idea: Same-side matching angles over a fixed base mean the spots share a curve.
question_patterns: Show that four spots with matching corners over one base, same side, sit on one curve.
Prove the concyclicity claim from the matching-angle condition.
Verify that A, B, X and Y share a curve given equal angles AXB and AYB.
Draw the case and check the matching-corner condition.
Explain why the side of the base matters in the claim.

solution_steps.action: Build the curve through three spots
solution_steps.explain: One curve passes uniquely through the non-lined-up spots A, B and C.

solution_steps.action: Rule out the fourth spot escaping
solution_steps.explain: If the fourth spot sat off the curve, its corner would differ, contradicting the given equality.
Since all four spots satisfy the equal-angle condition over the same base on the same side, they must lie on one common round curve, proving the four spots are concyclic.

concepts.title: Opposite Angles of a Cyclic Quadrilateral
concepts.definition: In a four-sided shape pinned on a round curve, each pair of facing corners adds up to 180 degrees.
concepts.key_idea: Facing corners are supplements: add either pair and get 180.
question_patterns: Find the corner facing a 75 degree corner in a pinned four-sided shape.
Calculate the missing facing corner when one is 110 degrees.
If angle P is (2x + 10) degrees and the facing angle R is (3x - 20) degrees, find x.
What do facing corners add to? State the reason.
Work out all four corners when two adjacent ones are 80 and 95 degrees.

solution_steps.explain: Facing corners of a pinned four-sided shape add to 180 degrees.
In a cyclic quadrilateral, each corner faces the one diagonally across, and the two together always sum to 180 degrees.
Adding the two facing corners gives 180 degrees, confirming the cyclic quadrilateral property that opposite angles are supplementary.
